item.title: ‘1619 Project’ professor Nikole Hannah-Jones pens tribute to convicted cop killer
item.description: Nikole Hannah-Jones, creator of the "1619 Project," is facing criticism for her tribute to the late Assata Shakur, who was convicted of killing a police officer and later labeled a terrorist by the FBI.

item.title: Top 5 game-changing higher ed reforms under Trump in 2025
item.description: The administration initiated investigations into antisemitism at universities, freezing funding for several institutions until the agreed to pay tens of millions of dollars and address discrimination.

item.title: ‘Hatecrimed five times in one night’ – here are the 31 campus hoaxes uncovered in 2025
item.description: Hate crimes, or hateful incidents, do occur. But in many cases, they are fake, lack important context, or even if they did occur, are hardly reasons to be worried.

item.title: Scholar: Boys kissing, ‘genderfluid pottery artists’ in kids’ lit make ‘better masculinity role models’
item.description: An Edinburgh Napier Univ. scholar highlights how boys kissing and diverse characters in children's literature can reshape masculinity. Adrianna Zabrzewska argues that addressing toxic masculinity through narratives fosters emotional expression and connection. Recommended books like "Two Boys Kissing" emphasize vulnerability and relationality, promoting better role models and challenging dominant gender norms.

item.title: What will happen to higher education in 2026? Our top predictions
item.description: OPINION/ANALYSIS The College Fix’s Gabrielle Temaat counts down The College Fix’s top predictions for 2026. From free speech battles and antisemitism to AI trends and academic reform, this upcoming year is poised to bring about even more change to the higher education landscape.

item.title: DEI crackdown, Charlie Kirk murder trial, and more: 5 stories we’ll be watching in 2026
item.description: The higher education landscape in 2026 will include key stories such as the Charlie Kirk murder trial, potential reforms to the left-dominated Truman Scholarship, skepticism towards higher education institutions, and on-going reforms by the Trump administration.
